Held FLAT: SBC is zero so there is nothing to expense or dilute; the ongoing buyback (RMB10.45M in H1 FY2026) is a small value-neutral count reduction and is not credited.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report: no share-based payment line in the P&L, cash flow statement or equity-award note; 'The Company has not adopted any share option scheme' (FY2024 AR p.6089, unchanged FY2025). SBC-zero market convention: rows kept explicit at 0%.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow RMB4.278M (FY2025 AR cash flow p.9015); a further RMB10.45M in H1 FY2026. Repurchaser, so the flat count is funded.
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724, Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T22:01Z; model values are computed in RMB and multiplied by 1.1724 to the HKD quote. No dual listing exists for a parity check; cross-check via pegs: USDHKD ~7.80 / USDCNY ~6.65 = 1.173, consistent. refresh_price.py does not move this rate -- re-derive it on any later refresh.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z regular HKEX close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in RMB, the currency of the flows: 10-year CGB ~1.8% risk-free + China ERP ~6.0% x beta 1.3 = ~9.6%, plus ~2.4pp size/liquidity premium for a HK-listed China micro-cap (market cap ~RMB450M, offshore holdco with contractual (VIE-type) arrangements over the PRC operating companies, 92% drawdown from IPO, thin float after the June-2025 unwind). WACC 12.0% on all three scenarios -- operating risk (AI payback, Baidu dependence, margin fragility) is carried in the scenario paths and weights, not in a per-scenario rate (charge risk once). Terminal growth 2.5% base, below China nominal GDP; terminal cap 12x owner FCF, the low end of the house range, because revenue is project/usage-based and the business is sub-scale.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal RMB3.465M + interest RMB0.315M = RMB3.78M in FY2025, 0.24% of revenue; H1 FY2026 RMB2.23M, 0.29%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 0.25%; lease liabilities (RMB8.431M at 30-Jun-2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (intangible amortisation ~RMB15M/yr + owned PPE ~RMB3.4M/yr).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are modelled on a consolidated basis; non-controlling interests deducted ONCE at book (RMB8.629M, 30-Jun-2026) in equity_bridge. NCI share of profit is immaterial (-RMB1.3M FY2025, +RMB1.0M H1 FY2026). Interests in associates (RMB8.700M) added at book because share of associate results sits below operating profit and is excluded from the flows (matching-asset rule).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (RMB flows / HKD quote bridge, lease treatment B, NCI + associate bridge, SBC-zero). Routed as an operating company (digital-health content/IT services for pharma and hospitals, pivoting to AI 'Digital Employee' agents); it is not a bank, REIT, holdco or distressed shell -- it is profitable with RMB217M net cash and no going-concern issue -- so the owner-FCF engine is the right route. The short history and volatile margins are handled inside the method rather than by a different model: (1) margins are anchored to the H1 FY2026 run-rate (EBITDA 2.9%, R&D 16.5% of revenue), not to the FY2025 peak (7.9%, which included RMB34.6M of capitalised software that H1 FY2026 expensed instead); (2) working capital is charged on the revenue change at -10% capture, which is why year-1 base owner FCF (~RMB8M, 0.4% of revenue) is far BELOW the FY2025 owner-FCF margin of 2.2% -- the FY2025 FCF is deliberately not carried forward; (3) the bear weight is raised to 35%. HISTORY READ: the FY2023/FY2024 net losses (-314M/-269M) were entirely fair-value changes on pre-IPO redemption liabilities (-325M/-273M, non-cash, terminated at listing); pre-redemption PBT was +RMB4M and +RMB9M, so the business was marginally profitable throughout, not a turnaround from operating losses. CAPITALISATION SHIFT: FY2024 purchased RMB75.3M of intangibles (software) with RMB97M R&D expensed; FY2025 RMB34.6M / RMB169M; H1 FY2026 nil / RMB127.6M. Total tech spend rose from 13% to 16.5% of revenue but moved wholesale from capex into opex -- the model treats EBITDA minus capex as the comparable series (FY2024 -2.0%, FY2025 5.7%, H1 FY2026 2.9%). INTEREST INCOME: stripped (RMB5.577M FY2025) because net cash of RMB217M is >6x the FCF base; the cash pile is credited once in the bridge. PRICE: at the recorded price the equity trades at ~RMB450M, roughly 2x net cash and ~2x FY2025 EBITDA. The chart shows a run from the HK$7.80 IPO to ~HK$55 in June 2025, a collapse to ~HK$8 within three weeks on 500-700M shares/week of volume (close to the whole share count), a grind lower through 2026 and a further halving in the first week of September 2026. Nothing in the filings through the H1 FY2026 interim (approved 28-Aug-2026) explains the September move. The model values the cash flows; the gap between the weighted IV and the price is the finding, and the candidate explanations the DCF cannot price -- controlling-shareholder or margin-financed forced selling, a cash-trap/VIE discount, undisclosed information -- are what the 35% bear weight and the key_risks list exist to flag. Treat the valuation as conditional on the reported cash being real and accessible.

equity_bridge.note: H1 FY2026 statement of financial position; associate results are below operating profit and excluded from the flows
H1 FY2026 statement of financial position; consolidated flows, NCI deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2028 growth (18% -> 12% deceleration from the H1 FY2026 +49.7% run-rate); the only computable historical CAGR, revenue 2-year (FY2023-FY2025) 12.05%, corroborates it
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Only three annual periods are available (FY2023-FY2025), so 3- and 5-year CAGRs cannot be computed. Equity and EPS CAGRs are undefined: FY2023 equity was negative (-RMB1,652M) because pre-IPO redemption liabilities sat in liabilities, and FY2023/FY2024 EPS were negative on the same non-cash fair-value charges. Owner FCF was negative in FY2023 and FY2024 (capitalised software spend exceeded OCF), so the FCF CAGR is also undefined. Revenue is the only usable series; the model does not lean on history for growth selection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (0) - interest income: FY2023 -35.476-0.683; FY2024 -19.544-1.118; FY2025 40.204-5.577. FY2024 revenue fell 3.5% (deprioritised consumer lines) before FY2025 +30.1% and H1 FY2026 +49.7%.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +30%: H1 was +49.7% (RMB775M); H2 FY2025 (RMB1,045M) is a much tougher comp, so H2 FY2026 at ~+20% gives ~RMB2.03bn. Decelerates to 3% by year 8 as content/RWS/IT project revenue matures and the AI line becomes a mid-single-digit share of revenue rather than a second engine.
base.margin_rationale: Post-IFRS16 EBITDA before the lease charge. Anchored to the H1 FY2026 run-rate (2.9%, with R&D at 16.5% of revenue and all tech spend expensed), not the FY2025 7.9% that included RMB34.6M of capitalised software. Matures to 7.5% as R&D intensity falls back toward 11-12% and selling expense (11.7% FY2025 -> 10.4% H1 FY2026) keeps leveraging. 7.5% EBITDA less 0.8% capex = 6.7% is ~1pp above FY2025's 5.7% EBITDA-minus-capex.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 P&L effective rate 8.4%, cash paid 4.4% (current tax liability building, RMB26.4M). Ramps from 10% to 15%: HNTE 15% rate (renewal expected end-2026) plus 100% R&D super-deduction keeps the blended rate below the 25% statutory; unrecognised tax losses are almost exhausted (RMB6.8M).
base.wc_rationale: Receivables 144 -> 291 -> 317 (FY2024 -> FY2025 -> H1 FY2026); CFO lagged EBITDA by ~13% of the revenue increase in FY2025 and ~11% in H1 FY2026. B2B pharma/hospital customers pay slowly; growth consumes cash.

bull.rationale: AI Digital Employee agents become a real second revenue line (tens of percent of revenue by FY2029) on top of continued 20-30% growth in content/RWS/IT services; R&D intensity falls back to ~10% as the product matures; software-like gross margin on AI revenue lifts group EBITDA to 11%. Working capital eases as enterprise AI contracts carry deposits (contract liabilities already RMB59M).

bear.rationale: AI R&D never pays back and is cut only after two more years of 15%+ R&D intensity; Baidu (18.2% of revenue, unilateral content pricing) trims page-view fees; pharma marketing compliance tightening shrinks content/RWS budgets; HNTE status lapses so cash tax rises to 22%; receivables keep absorbing cash. Margins stall at 4% -- roughly FY2025's operating margin -- on 2% growth.

scenario_narratives.base: Content/RWS and IT services for pharma companies and hospitals keep compounding off the hospital network (12,870 -> 17,047 in six months) and the 578 paying corporate customers, decelerating from the H1 FY2026 +50% to high single digits by FY2029. The AI Digital Employee line grows from ~2% of revenue but stays a feature of the IT-services offering rather than a second business. R&D intensity peaks in FY2026 and normalises toward 11-12% as revenue scales, letting EBITDA recover from the ~3% H1 FY2026 run-rate to 7.5% by FY2031. Growth consumes working capital at 10% of the revenue increase, so owner FCF is close to zero in FY2026 and builds thereafter. Cash tax ramps to 15% on the HNTE rate plus the R&D super-deduction.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI agents (medical assistants, health butlers, customised enterprise digital employees) convert the physician/hospital/pharma relationships into a scalable software line, with Baidu as distribution partner rather than price-setter; revenue grows 40%/28%/20% over FY2026-28 and the AI mix lifts group EBITDA to 11%. Enterprise contracts carry deposits so working-capital drag eases. Requires several independent things to go right -- AI commercial traction, Baidu alignment, margin discipline -- hence the 20% weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI pivot is an expensive narrative: R&D stays above 15% of revenue through FY2027 for a product that remains a low-single-digit share of sales, and is then cut back. Baidu reprices page-view content fees it sets unilaterally; pharma marketing compliance tightening and discretionary IT budgets slow growth to 2% from FY2029. HNTE status is not renewed, cash tax rises to 22%, and receivables keep absorbing cash. EBITDA stalls at 4%. This case also stands in for the governance/float risks the DCF cannot model: the June-2025 unwind that turned over nearly the whole share count in three weeks, the unexplained September-2026 halving, and the offshore-holdco access to RMB cash.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 35%: the investment thesis rests on an unproven pivot (AI R&D at 16.5% of revenue for ~2% of sales), there is a single-customer dependency (Baidu 18.2% of revenue, pricing set by Baidu, also a 10.9% shareholder), profitability is one year old and already compressed to a 1.4% operating margin, and the share price has fallen 92% from IPO with a September-2026 halving the filings do not explain -- a signal the market may hold information the model does not. Bull cut to 20% because it needs AI traction, Baidu alignment and margin discipline to coincide. Base 45% is the remainder.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A sub-scale but profitable China digital-health B2B platform (content, real-world-study support, IT services for pharma and hospitals) with RMB217M of net cash, zero SBC, a receivables-heavy working-capital cycle and an AI product line that currently costs far more than it earns. Value the owner cash flows the existing business can produce as R&D intensity normalises, charge working capital on growth, hold the share count flat, strip interest income and credit the cash once, and let a heavy bear weight carry the pivot, concentration and governance risks. The market is paying roughly net cash plus 2x EBITDA; the model's job is to say what the flows are worth and let the gap be the finding, not to back-solve the price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Reported cash (RMB232M, ~half the market cap) is held in PRC subsidiaries under an offshore holdco with contractual arrangements; the valuation credits it in full and is conditional on it being real and accessible to shareholders

Unexplained 92% price collapse since IPO including a ~50% fall in the first week of September 2026, after the H1 FY2026 interim; the June-2025 unwind traded ~700M shares/week against 877M in issue, consistent with margin-financed or controlling-shareholder forced selling -- information the filings do not contain
Baidu is 18.2% of revenue and sets content page-view fees unilaterally; it is also a 10.9% shareholder -- a renegotiation or exit is a two-sided hit

AI Digital Employee R&D (RMB128M in H1 FY2026, 16.5% of revenue) for ~2% of sales; the base case assumes intensity normalises -- if management keeps spending at this rate, EBITDA stays near 3% and the base IV falls toward the bear
Working capital: receivables RMB317M (~75 days) against B2B pharma/hospital customers; a collections problem would turn the thin positive FCF negative
Tax: HNTE 15% status expired end-2025 and renewal is pending; loss means 25% statutory rate (bear path)
China regulation of AI-assisted medical content, health data and pharma marketing sits directly on the revenue base
RMB/HKD: all flows in RMB against an HKD quote; a 5% RMB depreciation moves every HKD per-share value 5%
Thin liquidity after the 2025 unwind; the quoted price may not be achievable in size
